"Well that didn't go well" commented Greethus as the party returned to their lodgings burdened with paperwork.

"Actually it went as expected." Replied Trovita. "Phaedrus isn't really that oblivious, he just figured out that acting like it got him more respect. He'll examine your work once he's done whatever project has his attention right now and in the meantime he'll expect you to be too intimidated to bother him."

"So do we bother him?"

"No. He doesn't like feeling manipulated."

"But if we leave him alone and he helps us he won't feel manipulated."

"Yes." Trovita sighed. "I don't understand him well enough myself and I've been working with him for years. The Root isn't very helpful, just calls him a Path Nexus and tells me not to bother trying."

"Path Nexus?" Greethus felt the words resonate through him, touching something fundamental.

"That's one of the terms the Root uses for it." Trovita seemed distracted, looking at Greethus in a strange way. "I prefer it since I can almost understand what it means. The rest are things like *ta'veren* that aren't any language I recognize or stupid sounding things like protagonist. What sort of word is that anyways?" The last came out almost as a growl, but Greethus barely noticed. The words had shocked him, shaking him almost to bits. Acclimatizing to Sentenza was nothing compared to his current headache.

"Anyways, that's enough rambling. Get to work and when you're done I'll give you some copies of Phaedrus' work with remnant magic circuitry to examine for analogues and conversion opportunities. I figure the five of you should produce something at least comparable to what he will, after all you have a head start." Trovita dumped her stack of paperwork on a desk and drifted off, leaving Greethus with the other Illithid.

*The other Illithid.* And that's what they were. Completely generic, not even names. Oh, they had names when Greethus thought of them, for instance that one with the short tentacles was named Theegle, but not until Greethus thought of them. And if he didn't concentrate, the names and features changed the next time he thought of them! *They were defined by their interactions with him.*

Leaving Theegle and the other Illithid to their paperwork, Greethus stumbled off after Trovita. As he reached the doorway to her office he stopped, hearing her speaking to someone. He peaked through the door, and saw something very strange.

Standing in front of Trovita's desk was a creature that could be best described as a humanoid plant. It was soaked with water, dripping all over the floor, and yet it was still frequently taking swigs from a canteen. Most striking though were they eyes. The reflected the room perfectly, seeming to take no light at all into them, yet the creature could still see the crystal Trovita was handing it somehow.

"Took me far too long to find this" Trovita was griping. "The thing has no power left and was buried deep in that forest, took me so long to find it I had to make up a story about having trouble with moonlight for those stupid Illithid! And that's not even mentioning all the creepy centipedes trying to mate with me while I was looking for the damned thing!"

"Well did you?" The creature spoke in a careful, measured way.

"Did I what?"

"Mate with any of them?"

"What! No I did not! That is-"

"A pity, that would truly be a unique experience"

Trovita stood speechless for a time before hurling a paperweight at the creature. "Just get out!" she shrieked.

The creature caught the paperweight in one hand without any visible effort, and lightly tossed it back onto the papers it had been holding down before they could flutter too far away. Even as it did so it stepped out of Trovita's office, still holding the strange crystal. Greethus pushed himself against the wall, but the creature took no notice of him as it strode quickly out of the building. Greethus quickly returned to Theegle and the others, thinking on what he had heard. So they were 'stupid Illithid' were they? They would show her!

Returning from their meeting with Phaedrus, buried under they paperwork that is a consequence of bureaucracy, the Illithid return feeling the meeting had gone poorly, only to be informed that it's Phaedrus' way of ensuring he will not be bothered. Upon having some meta realizations, Greethus decides to speak with Trovita, only to see a SeaFair Ackermann speaking with her, discussing the Crystal of Reflection. The Illithid over hear an insult, and decides to show Trovita exactly how "stupid" they were.
